title: Moving to New York and surviving lean times
summary: He says he fell into the Wonder job, later made it through lean times in the early 90s and never held a lasting non-music job.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: how I was going to do it, you know, so I just like I fell into that Stevie Wonder gig. And the funny thing is I went from one to another and the cost of living was nothing like it is now. God, like I don’t know how people do it now. I mean you’ve certainly got to make a lot of money going out of school. So I went to New York, and the hardest times were when some lean times hit, like in the early 90s or something, where I never did the thing where I’d do other gigs to figure out how to do it. I remember once I had a girlfriend and she was doing proofreading. And she said, “You know you could do proofreading, or do it at night, and you don’t have to be concerned about someone seeing you do something else.” So I thought yeah, I’ve got to do something that gets me through the slow period. So it was a two part course in proofreading. So I went to take the first part. After that I got so busy I never took the second. Once I saw that I said okay I’m going to do whatever I have to do to make things work.
So you’ve never had any long term, non-music gigs?
No. When I came home from college I worked in a deli or something, but I quit that.
